newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks finish week at all-time highs.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks finish week at all-time highs.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended the week at all-time highs on Friday, boosted by a rally in bonds, dollar * Bank, energy, base metals led 10 of 14 groups higher * 92 million shares traded
Toronto stocks closed the week at record highs on Friday, joining a currency and bond rally on the back of favorable Canadian trade numbers.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 18.45 points to 5492.60, surpassing the previous record close set on Wednesday.
The key index also hit an intra-day peak of 5494.57.
Trading was brisk with 92.01 million shares exchanging hands for a value of C$1.4 billion.
Financial markets rallied after Statistics Canada reported that Canada's trade surplus jumped to a record high in August amid surging exports to the United States.
Canada's trade surplus rose to a record C$4.02 billion in August from C$2.89 billion in July, prompting economists to predict another current account surplus in the third quarter.
In today's action, the TSE's 10 strong groups included base metals, banking, energy and transportation. The four weak sectors included heavy losses in consumer products and gold.

Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 523 to 436 with 282 issues unchanged. "Fundamentally, you have a market that wants to go higher," said John Kellett, vice-president of equities for Royal Bank of Canada.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Edper Group receipts topped the most active list, jumping 11.30 to 63 on 6.3 million shares. Edper's class A stock gained 0.65 to 6 after hitting a 52-week high of 6.30 on its merger with brother firm, Hees International Bancorp.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd regained some its losses this week caused by a dispute over the ownership of its huge Indonesian gold discovery. Bre-X closed up 2 at 21.90 as bargain hunters picked up the stock, traders said.
* Midland Walwyn Inc jumped 2.10 to 12.75 on 463,000 shares amid rumors that Bank of Nova Scotia may be eyeing the independent brokerage firm. Both firms denied the rumors.
